prompt.context: Your client is MBS Co., a government sponsored enterprise (GSE), that purchases mortgages from banks, packages them into mortgage-backed securities (MBS), and sells them in the secondary market to investors. MBS Co.'s return on capital (ROC) has declined since last year, and the management team is looking for your help in understanding why this has happened and how to improve ROC going forward.
prompt.question: Why has MBS Co.'s return on capital declined since last year, and what can management do to improve ROC going forward?

clarifying_info.q: How does MBS Co. make money?
clarifying_info.a: MBS Co. keeps a small fee on each mortgage payment that passes through, based on a percentage of mortgage volume. The fee percent is consistent for all mortgages regardless of riskiness and has been consistent since last year.

MBS Co. has one other GSE competitor. The securities from both are fungible to investors. Banks can also hold mortgages rather than sell to a GSE. No new competitors have entered; the government only allows MBS Co. and its one competitor to create MBS.
When a homeowner makes a monthly mortgage payment, it passes through the bank first, then through MBS Co., then to investors (primarily institutional investors).
There is no target ROC. Any improvement in ROC would be considered a success. ROC = profits / capital.

clarifying_info.q: Have regulations or market conditions changed?
clarifying_info.a: Regulations have not changed. All market conditions have remained consistent since last year.

exhibits.title: 2017 Mortgage Originations
exhibits.shows: A stacked bar chart showing portfolio composition by capital requirement cohort for MBS Co., Competitor A, and banks (held on bank portfolios) in 2017. X-axis: percent of mortgage volume. Y-axis: breakdown across four cohorts. Capital requirement = cash a company must hold as a percent of mortgage securitization volume, based on FICO score and loan-to-value ratio.

data.note: Portfolio compositions were roughly the same for MBS Co., Competitor A, and banks in 2017

exhibits.title: 2018 Mortgage Originations
exhibits.shows: Same stacked bar chart structure as Exhibit 1 but for 2018 mortgage originations. Shows how market share and portfolio mix changed year-over-year across MBS Co., Competitor A, and banks.

notes: Total market size in dollars has remained consistent
Total market composition of mortgages by cohort has remained consistent
Each company's percent in the 0.5-1.0% and 1.0-2.0% cohorts is consistent between years

exhibits.title: 2019F Securitization Portfolio
exhibits.shows: A table showing MBS Co.'s 2019 forecasted securitization portfolio with four capital requirement cohorts plus a total row. Columns: capital requirement cohort, securitization volume ($B), capital ($B), cohort ROC.

framework: ROC = Profit / Capital -- framework must identify both profit and capital as separate components; a standard profit tree alone is insufficient
Profit drivers: mortgage riskiness / borrower creditworthiness, pricing pressure from banks, fee pressure from investors, internal costs
Capital drivers: regulatory capital requirements by cohort, excess cash build-up, build-up of unsecuritizable mortgages
Market context (not controllable levers): interest rates / yield curve, oversupply of housing, consumer housing preferences
Competition: new entrants, competitor pricing/fees, customer/supplier vertical integration (banks holding mortgages)

questions.prompt: Using Exhibits 1 and 2, what changed between 2017 and 2018 that could explain MBS Co.'s decline in ROC?
questions.guidance: Strong answer identifies: (1) MBS Co. and Competitor A lost market share to banks in 2018; (2) MBS Co.'s portfolio shifted toward higher capital requirement cohorts (>2%); (3) Banks' portfolio shifted toward lower capital requirement cohorts (<0.5%); (4) Key insight: banks are earlier in the value chain and can cherry-pick low capital requirement mortgages to hold, passing high capital requirement loans to MBS Co. Higher capital held against the same profits equals lower ROC.

questions.prompt: The client has identified a way for 10% of the capital backing high capital requirement mortgages (>2% cohort) to be redeployed in low capital requirement loans (<0.5% cohort). Using Exhibit 3, how much will this shift change overall ROC?
questions.guidance: Candidate should first recognize directionally that moving capital from a 4% ROC cohort to a 25% ROC cohort will increase overall ROC. Securitization volume is a red herring -- not needed for the calculation. Cohort ROC does not change as a result of the capital shift. Two valid solution methods exist. New ROC = 12.5% (up ~0.5pp from 12.0%). Second-order insight: shifting capital to lower capital requirement loans requires increasing total portfolio size and thus market share.

math.setup: 10% of >2.0% cohort capital = 10% x $5.0B = $0.5B shifted from >2.0% cohort to <0.5% cohort. Total capital remains $20B.
steps: Method 1 (incremental): Change in dollar returns = (+$0.5B x 25.0%) + (-$0.5B x 4.0%) = +$125M - $20M = +$105M
Method 2 (full rebuild): New capital by cohort: <0.5%=$2.5B, 0.5-1.0%=$8.0B, 1.0-2.0%=$5.0B, >2.0%=$4.5B, Total=$20.0B
math.answer: New ROC = 12.5%, an increase of approximately 0.5 percentage points from current 12.0%

brainstorming.prompt: What methods can MBS Co. use to shift its portfolio to higher ROC (lower capital requirement) loans?

categories.name: Homeowners
ideas: Build preference for MBS Co. with high-quality borrowers by simplifying the mortgage process
Improve screening/selection process to better identify high-quality borrowers

categories.name: Banks
ideas: Build preference to sell to MBS Co. by simplifying the mortgage process
Lower fees to entice banks to sell high-quality mortgages rather than hold them on portfolio
Form partnerships with banks to bolster flow of high-quality mortgages to securitization

categories.name: MBS Co. (internal)
ideas: Bypass banks and begin originating mortgages directly with consumers
Expand into other geographic regions (e.g., non-US markets)
Expand into other types of loans (e.g., student loans, car loans)

categories.name: Government
ideas: Lobby government to lower capital requirements for certain cohorts
Request government capital infusion to fund more high-ROC mortgage purchases

recommendation: MBS Co.'s ROC has declined because banks are choosing to hold high-quality (low capital requirement) mortgages on their own portfolios and passing high capital requirement loans to MBS Co., shifting MBS Co.'s portfolio mix toward lower-ROC cohorts

MBS Co. can increase ROC by approximately 0.5 percentage points to 12.5% by redeploying capital from its >2% cohort into its <0.5% cohort, achievable via a chosen idea from the brainstorm (e.g., forming bank partnerships or lowering fees to attract high-quality mortgage flow)
risks: Risks depend on chosen idea: aggressive fee changes may upset bank relationships; direct-to-consumer origination requires capabilities MBS Co. may not currently have
Shifting to lower capital requirement loans requires increasing total portfolio size and market share, which may be difficult given banks' incentive to retain good loans
Expansion into new loan types or geographies introduces execution risk and regulatory complexity
next_steps: Conduct feasibility and cost-benefit assessment of top 2-3 portfolio shift ideas
Pilot with a subset of bank partners or in a new geographic region
Track portfolio composition quarterly to ensure mix shifts toward lower capital requirement cohorts
